title: Hostinger AI Builder (formerly Horizons): is it worth it, or WordPress?
seoTitle: Is Hostinger Horizons worth it? A site without coding
description: Hostinger's AI Builder, the former Horizons, suits a simple website or app without coding; if you want plugins and control, stay with WordPress.
metaDescription: Hostinger Horizons is now the AI Builder. Is it worth it, or should you use WordPress? A table by project type, a comparison with Wix and Lovable, and AI credits.
imageAlt: Hostinger logo and the AI Builder, the former Horizons, going head to head with WordPress

contentSections.heading: Quick answer
paragraphs: Hostinger's AI Builder, the former Horizons, is worth it if you want a simple website or web app without coding and you're fine with the AI building the first version. If you need plugins, your own theme and full control, WordPress is the better fit. What decides it is the type of project; the table is below.

contentSections.heading: What the AI Builder is (the former Horizons)
paragraphs: Horizons was Hostinger's AI builder for websites and apps. In 2026 it merged with the traditional website builder and became the AI Builder (Hostinger AI Builder): the old address redirects to the new page. Searches still use the old name, which is why it appears here.
The page says it creates websites and web apps from a text description, with no technical knowledge, in two modes:
bullets: **Editing without AI (Manual mode):** you start with a site generated by the AI or with one of the templates and edit by dragging and dropping. It uses no AI credits.
**Editing with AI (Agentic mode):** you describe what you want in the chat and the AI designs and codes it. Every action uses AI credits, and you can top them up.
postParagraphs: What comes out is a website or a web app, not an app for the App Store or Google Play: the page says so itself. Hosting, domain and email come with the plan, and the source code can be exported to host elsewhere. All of this is Hostinger's own description.

Don't confuse it with Hostinger's automation agents, such as OpenClaw and Hermes Agent: those are [assistants that run on a server](/en/reviews/openclaw-vs-hermes-agent) and reply on Telegram or WhatsApp. The AI Builder builds the website.

contentSections.heading: Which project it suits: the table
paragraphs: The right question isn't "is the AI good?" but "what am I going to build, and who will work on it afterwards?". The table sums up the choice by project type, based on what the AI Builder page and the WordPress documentation say:

rows: Menu, restaurant or services page
AI Builder
A few pages, text and photos. The AI builds it, and the mode without AI uses no credits for tweaks.
Portfolio or résumé
AI Builder
The gallery has ready-made templates for this, and the Premium plan is enough.
Small store with a few products
AI Builder (Unlimited plan) or WordPress with WooCommerce
The AI Builder offers an online store as a paid add-on; WooCommerce gives more control over shipping and payment, but needs setup.
Blog that depends on plugins (SEO, forms, members area)
WordPress
The catalog of plugins and themes belongs to WordPress; in the AI Builder, every new function is something the AI has to build.
Web app: scheduling, client portal, simple CRM
AI Builder (AI mode)
The page promises a built-in back end, login and database. In WordPress that turns into plugins and a developer.
Project that someone else or an agency will maintain
WordPress
It's the market standard: any professional knows how to work with it.

postParagraphs: If your project fits in two lines, start with the AI Builder: it has a free trial, no card, with 5 AI credits. If what you need already has a plugin name, go with WordPress.

contentSections.heading: AI Builder or WordPress
paragraphs: At Hostinger, the price of the hosting plan doesn't decide it: the AI Builder's no-AI mode comes with the same plans that run WordPress, at the same prices. The AI mode uses credits, and to publish the site you need active hosting. What changes is who does the work and what you control.

postParagraphs: **WordPress wins** when the project depends on a specific plugin, on a theme you already have, or on someone who will maintain the site later. It is free software: the whole site is yours and moves to any host without rework.

**The AI Builder wins** when you don't want to install or update anything and you want a web app with login and data, which in WordPress becomes a stack of plugins. The caveat that changes the decision: in AI mode, every change uses credits. According to the page, a simple institutional page uses 5 to 10 credits, and a more complex app, 15 or more. Anyone who changes the site every week has to do the math. Anyone who builds it once and edits text and photos in the no-AI mode's editor uses none; in AI mode, even swapping a text or an image with Select & edit uses a few credits.

contentSections.heading: AI Builder or Wix (and Lovable)
paragraphs: Wix is the traditional drag-and-drop builder, with its own hosting. It has a free plan on a Wix address, and a custom domain needs a paid plan. If you want a pure visual editor, Wix does the job. If what matters is being able to take the project away later, compare by what each page guarantees: the AI Builder's page says the code can be exported, and WordPress is free software that moves to any host.

Lovable is another vibe-coding tool, the same idea as the AI Builder's AI mode: you describe, the AI codes. The difference is in the package. Lovable charges by credits, per message, and has a free plan with a few credits a day; it is the tool for building, and you sort out domain and email separately. At Hostinger, hosting, domain and email come in the same plan, and the mode without AI uses no credits. For someone who already codes and wants only the AI, Lovable is comparable; for someone who wants everything in one place, Hostinger.

contentSections.heading: What to check before paying
bullets: **The credits.** AI mode uses credits on every request, and the plan's balance doesn't renew every month. Even swapping a text or an image with Select & edit uses a few; only the no-AI mode edits for free.
**What happens if you don't renew.** The page warns: a plan that expires without renewal takes the project offline and deletes the data. Export the code before letting it expire.
**30-day refund**, as long as you have used fewer than 30 AI credits.
**The online store** is a paid add-on, available on the Unlimited and Cloud Startup plans and billed separately from the plan. Check its price at checkout.
**There is no native app.** What the AI Builder makes is a responsive web app, which opens in the phone's browser. For the App Store and Google Play, it's a different path.
postParagraphs: How Hostinger bills, renews and refunds is covered in [Is Hostinger trustworthy?](/en/reviews/is-hostinger-legit).

contentSections.heading: Is it worth it? The verdict
paragraphs: **It's worth it** if you want a site of a few pages, a portfolio, a small store or a simple web app and you don't want to code or look after plugins. The first version comes from the description, and the mode without AI lets you tweak without spending credits. Start with the free trial; if the result works for you, the Premium plan covers a simple site and Unlimited covers a store.

**Stay with WordPress** if the project depends on plugins, on a theme of your own, on someone who will maintain the site, or if you want to move everything to another host without rework. The Hostinger plan is the same in both cases, so the choice is only about the tool.
**If in doubt, try the AI Builder before paying.** You get 5 free credits, no card, enough to see whether the AI understands what you want. If it doesn't, WordPress is still there.

contentSections.heading: Frequently asked questions
bullets: Does Hostinger Horizons still exist? It exists under another name. In 2026 Horizons merged with Hostinger's website builder and became the AI Builder (Hostinger AI Builder), with a drag-and-drop mode and a mode for building through the chat. The old address redirects to the new page.

Does Hostinger's AI Builder build the site on its own? It builds the first version from your description, according to the page. The content, the photos and the business decisions are still yours, and every request in AI mode uses credits.
Do you need to know how to code to use the AI Builder? No. The page says it requires no technical knowledge in either mode. For people who do code, AI mode has a code editor.

Can you migrate from the AI Builder to another host? The page says the source code can be exported and hosted elsewhere. The built-in back end, with database and login, stays at Hostinger, so an app needs reconfiguring outside it.

Is the AI Builder good for an online store? For a small store, yes: the online store is available on the Unlimited and Cloud Startup plans as a paid add-on. For a large store, with shipping and payment rules, WordPress with WooCommerce gives more control.

takeIf: Take the AI Builder if you want a site of a few pages, a portfolio, a small store or a simple web app without coding.
Take it if you want hosting, domain and email in the same plan and you're fine with the AI building the first version.
Take it if you'll build the site once and tweak text and photos in the no-AI mode's editor, which uses no credits.
skipIf: Skip it, and stay with WordPress, if the project depends on a specific plugin or on a theme you already have.
Skip it if someone else or an agency will maintain the site: WordPress is the market standard.
Skip it if you want to move everything to another host without rework, or if you'll ask the AI for changes every week and each request uses credits.
